summary: Defines the DNSSEC Lookaside Validation resource record, for publishing DNSSEC trust anchors outside the DNS delegation chain. It is informational and is now historic.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo defines a DNS record for trust information stored outside the usual chain of DNS delegations. It explains where the record may appear and why it must be authenticated.

questions: what is the dnssec lookaside validation record
how is a dlv record different from ds
why must dlv data be authenticated
subtitle: A DNS record format for publishing DNSSEC trust anchors outside the delegation chain.

tldr.problem: A DNSSEC validation chain may be unavailable when an ancestor zone is unsigned or does not publish a delegation signer record for a child.
tldr.mechanism: The DLV resource record provides a way to publish trust-anchor data outside the normal DNS delegation chain, using the same format and algorithm registries as DS.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4431 is Historic. It defines the DLV record's format and cautions that software using it for validation must authenticate it.

today: RFC 4431 is marked Historic in the unit metadata. It defines the DLV resource record and its security considerations.

sections.title: Trust Outside the Delegation Chain
sections.content:
DNSSEC authenticates DNS data by building a chain of public-key signatures along DNS delegations from a trust anchor. The DLV resource record provides a way to publish trust-anchor data outside that chain.

The RFC expects such records to help validators reach signed data when an ancestor zone is not signed or does not publish a Delegation Signer (DS) record for a child. How validators use DLV records is outside this document's scope.
sections.plainLanguage: DNSSEC normally follows signed delegations from a trusted starting point. DLV provides another place to publish trust data when a link in that path is missing.

sections.title: The DLV Resource Record
sections.content:
The DLV record has the same wire and presentation formats as the DS record defined in RFC 4034. It reuses the same algorithm and digest type values. IANA assigned DLV DNS type code 32769.

DLV is a normal DNS record type without DS-specific processing rules. Unlike DS, it may not appear on the parent side of a zone cut, but it may appear at a zone apex.
sections.plainLanguage: DLV uses the same data layout as DS but has its own record type and placement rules. It can appear at the top of a zone.

sections.title: Authenticating DLV Data
sections.content:
For servers and resolvers that do not use DLV records in DNSSEC validation, DLV records are ordinary DNS data and the memo identifies no particular security concern. Software that does use DLV for validation will need constraints on how it accepts those records.

The RFC says using DLV without cryptographic authentication would be unwise. Failure to authenticate it could make spoofed DNS data harder to detect. It also notes that a key tag helps select DNSKEY records but does not uniquely identify a key.
sections.plainLanguage: A validator must check that DLV information is genuine before relying on it. A key tag alone may not identify one unique key.
